surprises.description: Cincinnati Financial’s combined ratio was 90.9%, about 5 points better than the preview’s roughly 96% back-solved expectation. That outperformance came despite catastrophe losses adding 7 points year over year to the ratio.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The property casualty combined ratio rose 2.7 points to 90.9%, driven by a 7.0-point increase in catastrophe losses.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “a $2.00 consensus implies roughly a 96% combined ratio”

surprises.description: Operating income held nearly flat year over year: $443 million, down just $6 million, even though after-tax catastrophe losses were $146 million higher. That was much more resilient than the preview’s consensus-based expectation of a 28%–30% decline in operating EPS.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating income was $443 million, down only $6 million year-over-year despite catastrophe losses being $146 million higher after-tax.”

surprises.description: Cincinnati Global’s combined ratio improved sharply to 70.7%, versus the preview’s 110.8% figure for the segment. Its 13% premium growth accompanied a much stronger underwriting result than the preview’s description of Global as a persistent drag suggested.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Global: 110.8% CR ($10M Saudi loss, $7.5M event-cancellation reserve)”; “Global has been a persistent drag.”

surprises.description: Cincinnati Re’s premiums grew 34%, well above the preview’s 16% growth figure, but its 94.8% combined ratio was substantially worse than the preview’s 87.6%. The segment delivered faster growth alongside weaker underwriting than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cincinnati Re grew net written premiums 34% (94.8% combined ratio).”

surprises.description: The quarter’s value-creation result and book value were much weaker than the preview’s estimate: the value creation ratio was negative 2.1%, and book value was $105.42 per share versus an estimated $112–$116. The roughly $1.2 billion pretax bond-portfolio loss from rising rates was the stated driver.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Rising interest rates caused a roughly $1.2 billion pretax net loss on the bond portfolio, pushing the quarterly value creation ratio to negative 2.1%”; “book value at $105.42 per share.”

surprises.description: Cincinnati Financial repurchased only an immaterial number of shares despite holding $6.1 billion in cash and marketable securities. That was a notable pullback from the $216 million of repurchases in Q2 while the preview specifically highlighted the pace of buybacks as a question at the current share price.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The parent company held $6.1 billion in cash and marketable securities … and repurchased only an immaterial number of shares.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Buyback pace: 1.3M shares @ $161.93 = $216M in Q2”; “Pace at ~$175 tests management’s own valuation view.”

surprises.description: Renewal pricing was at the low end of the preview’s framing: Commercial Lines and E&S were in the low single digits, rather than the preview’s cited high end of the low-single-digit range. That points to somewhat less pricing support for future commercial margins than the preview’s central expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Renewal price increases decelerated, with Commercial Lines and E&S in the low single digits.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Commercial renewal pricing: ‘High end of the low single-digit percentage range.’”

surprises.description: Net favorable prior-year reserve development was stronger than the preview’s roughly 2-point favorable base assumption, benefiting the combined ratio by 3.6 points. Commercial casualty had no material development, though $56 million of adverse development from pre-2024 accident years tempered the favorable result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “$94 million of net favorable prior-year reserve development (benefiting the combined ratio by 3.6 points), but commercial casualty saw no material development and $56 million of adverse development came from pre-2024 accident years.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base … PYD ~2 pts favorable”; the preview also flagged a commercial casualty reserve charge as a key downside risk.

surprises.description: The nine-month current accident-year combined ratio excluding catastrophes improved to 86.5% from 86.7%, showing slightly better underlying performance than the preview’s concern about deterioration in the clean ex-cat measure. This is a nine-month figure, rather than the standalone Q3 ratio the preview identified as the key test.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The 9-month current accident year combined ratio excluding catastrophes improved slightly to 86.5% from 86.7%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Current accident year ex-cat combined ratio … The cleanest signal of underlying margin. Deterioration here in a soft market is the real bear case.”

surprises.description: Management reported that AI-enabled automation accelerated new-business submission processing by more than 30% across Commercial Lines and E&S. The preview discussed the expense-ratio target but did not anticipate this operating-efficiency progress.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AI-enabled automation has accelerated new business submission processing by more than 30% across Commercial Lines and E&S, supporting the goal of keeping the commercial lines expense ratio under 30%.”
